title: Scalable Temporal Motif Densest Subnetwork Discovery

problem.claim: Discovering subnetworks that are dense according to edges or higher-order structures, including subgraphs or k-cliques, constitutes a fundamental algorithmic problem with many applications.

gap.claim: Although dense-subnetwork discovery has been studied extensively in static networks, substantial questions remain for temporal networks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dense-subnetwork discovery is a fundamental algorithmic problem with applications and can use edges or complex structures.
Temporal-network versions of the problem remain substantially less explored than static-network versions.

source_observation.claim: Dense-subnetwork discovery can be defined over increasingly complex network structures, including subgraphs and k-cliques.

interpretation.claim: A useful formulation should make the density structure explicit rather than assuming edge density is the only objective.

application.claim: When analyzing temporal networks, consider density objectives based on motifs or other higher-order structures.

exception.claim: The supplied units do not specify which temporal structures, datasets, or application settings are appropriate.

unknowns: The proposed method or algorithm is not described.
Temporal motif definition and density objective are not specified.
Scalability claims, experiments, datasets, and quantitative results are not provided.
